title: differentiated-queue-lattice-and-kernel-fit-probe-controller
creator: Asha Patel
description: Problem: SLO violations from long-tail requests during mixed workloads. Existing admission controllers are single-policy and over-prioritize throughput, leading to kernel mismatches (heavy attention kernels selected for short-prefill bursts) and tail latency spikes. Goal: Implement a differentiated queue lattice with SLA-tiered slices and an active kernel-fit probing controller that steers admission decisions and kernel selection together to reduce p99/p99.9 for latency-sensitive tenants while preserving overall throughput for best-effort workloads.
acceptance_criteria: P99 latency for latency-tier (gold) tenants reduced by >= 30% under synthetic mixed load compared to baseline
No more than 5% throughput regression for best-effort workloads at 95th percentile load
Kernel-fit probe identifies at least two misclassified request shapes per minute per node during 95th percentile traffic and triggers fallback policy
End-to-end e2e tests demonstrating admission hysteresis prevents oscillation for at least 10 minutes under bursty arrivals
Feature flags and rollout knobs present (per-customer tiering, probe frequency, hysteresis window) and documented in console
design_notes: Queue lattice: logically slice the admission queue into deterministic lanes (gold, silver, bronze) with per-lane pacing tokens. Each lane exposes a soft budget to the central scheduler and enforces a max fill rate to protect latency SLOs.

Kernel-fit probing: lightweight micro-probes run at admission time to sample request shape (seq length, prompt history, attention density heuristic). Probes are constant-time checks (no full prefill) that map request to a kernel suitability score (fast/medium/heavy). Probes are probabilistic (sample rate configurable) to limit overhead.

Admission decision combines lane priority, current lane budget, kernel-fit score, and node kernel-availability hint. If kernel-fit indicates heavy kernel but node lacks optimized kernel path, route to fallback (smaller batch, different kernel path, or deferred admission) depending on SLA tier.
Hysteresis & backoff: to avoid oscillation when capacities change rapidly, implement exponential hysteresis windows per-lane learned from recent admission outcomes (successful vs. slow).

Telemetry: record per-request lane, kernel-fit score, chosen kernel path, admission delay, and decode latency. Expose derived metrics: misclassification-rate, fallback-rate, lane-starvation incidents.
Compatibility: works with existing KV cache and streaming flow. Prefill probe reads only header metadata and first token vector norms (no payload copies).
implementation_steps: Spike (done): 2-day experiment to prototype kernel-fit heuristic in colocated process (results in comments)
Step 1: Add lane-aware admission queue data structures and per-lane token buckets (scheduler changes, ~3 days)
Step 2: Implement kernel-fit probe module (C++ runtime + Rust shim; proto interface with 99% fast-path latency under 50us) (~4 days)
Step 3: Admission policy engine that combines lane budget + kernel-fit score + node hint; implement fallback strategies (defer, smaller batch, route) (~4 days)
Step 4: Integrate hysteresis window and learning (tuneable parameters, default conservative) (~2 days)
Step 5: Instrumentation + dashboards (console route metrics, per-tenant p99, probe telemetry) (~3 days)
Step 6: Canary rollout behind feature flag (10% of gold then expand), collect metrics, iterate (~2 weeks)
Step 7: Full rollout with automatic rollback thresholds (if p99 increases for gold or throughput falls beyond threshold)
metrics: p50/p90/p99/p99.9 latency by lane and node
kernel-misclassification-rate (% requests where probe indicated fast but heavy kernel used)
lane-starvation counts and average queue wait times
rollout_plan: Stage 0: Internal dark launch in dev cluster, telemetry only (current)
Stage 1: Canary (10% of gold traffic), monitor for 48 hours. Auto-roll back on p99 regression > 10% or throughput loss > 7%
Stage 2: Expand to 30% gold + 5% silver; validate misclassification and fallback rates
Stage 3: 100% gold, 50% silver, bronze opt-in; keep feature flag for emergency disable
Stage 4: Post-rollout 30-day observation and parameter tuning using traffic data
risks: Probe overhead added to admission path could increase median latency if implemented incorrectly
Misclassification can cause unnecessary fallbacks and throughput loss—need conservative defaults
Complexity increases in scheduler could introduce bugs leading to lane starvation for non-gold tenants
Interaction with KV cache warm/cold state might skew kernel-fit heuristics—need validation that probe does not read cache state directly
Operational burden: new metrics/dashboards require runbook updates and alert tuning
test_plan: Unit tests for kernel-fit scoring logic with synthetic request shapes
Integration tests for queue lattice under deterministic arrival traces (replay historical production traces)
Load test: mixed workload (50% small chat, 30% large-context completions, 20% embeddings) at 120% baseline QPS to validate tail behavior
Chaos test: simulate kernel eviction and node degradation, ensure hysteresis prevents oscillation
Canary A/B: compare p99/p99.9 across control and experiment groups with bootstrap confidence intervals
